name: gen5_fp8_ncu_profile
description: FP8->FP16 WMMA fallback GEMM. FP8 input loaded from global, converted to FP16 in shared memory, then HMMA FP16->FP32 tensor core multiply.
note: FP8 input -> FP16 WMMA fallback with HMMA activity. tcgen05.mma (native FP8 tensor core) requires SM 100/103/110 and is NOT available on SM 120. Benefit is FP8 input bandwidth reduction, not native FP8 compute throughput.

analysis.primary_bottleneck: DRAM bandwidth — only 0.94% of peak read throughput at 1024, 0.86% at 4096
analysis.tensor_utilization: Low — 11.85% at 1024, 15.39% at 4096. Kernel is memory-bound, not compute-bound
analysis.top_stall: Long scoreboard (15.57% at 1024, 13.26% at 4096) — warps waiting for shared memory load dependencies
analysis.scaling: Larger size improves occupancy (76%->85%) and tensor utilization (12%->15%) but kernel remains bandwidth-limited
analysis.fp8_advantage: FP8 input halves DRAM read vs FP16 (4MB vs 8MB for 1024x1024 matrix), but conversion to FP16 in shared memory negates compute savings since HMMA operates on FP16
analysis.vs_cublaslt: cuBLASLt achieves 43-138 TFLOPS vs our 4-6 TFLOPS. cuBLASLt uses optimized tiling, prefetching, and possibly HMMA with higher arithmetic intensity

convergence.claim: FP8->FP16 WMMA fallback kernel profiled with ncu at 1024 and 4096. Primary bottleneck is DRAM bandwidth (0.86-0.94% of peak read). Tensor core utilization is 12-15%. Long scoreboard stalls dominate (13-16%). cuBLASLt FP8 outperforms by 10-30x due to higher arithmetic intensity.
convergence.label: FP8_NCU_PROFILED
